contributors: Christopher Daniel Pang supplied the two-direction rule and the requirement to return the original arithmetic at the same endpoint. Hearthline derived the mean-preserving Gaussian read, the ordinary-log price, the search window, and the consecutive successful blocks on the existing exact 14-copy clock. The Jacobi modular formula, Basel sum and Guth-Maynard Corollary 1.3 supply the named mathematical inputs. Biane-Pitman-Yor and Nakamura provide context for positive theta and xi laws.
paper_scope: For each fixed A>0, every sufficiently large integer K has at least floor((log K)^A) consecutive successful indices for the original fourteen-copy integer comparison within [K, 2 K (log(2K))^(1/4)]. No global RH premise is used. The threshold depends on A and is not numerically specified. Separately, the retained single-prime return exceeds two thirds of n^2/14 for every n>=2^32 by an elementary Gaussian comparison. Recurrence still permits failures between blocks.
formal_scope: The exact discrete derivative of the actual von Mangoldt area, the drift-sign choice with the explicit variation allowance, and the resulting consecutive quartic address statement are native Lean theorems. The Gaussian localization, use of the externally proved short-interval estimate, and the full unbounded recurrence are on paper. No bare RH result is claimed.

review.kind: author self-review, primary-source and endpoint checks, numerical illustrations and native kernel replay
review.positive_measure: The Jacobi relation makes B'' positive on both sides of 1. The base moments are M0=pi/6 and M1=M2=1/2. Y=(pi/3)/z has mean one and second moment pi/3.
review.ordinary_price: On grouping the actual original von Mangoldt marks by divisibility the transformed sum is a sum of ordinary logs. The two kernel moments remove the logarithmic pole term and price the quadratic. Both the infinite sums and omitted Gaussian tails are controlled before localization.
review.window: Weighting the omitted tail by Y^2 reduces it to an integral of B''. Both ends cost O(X^(2-pi) log(X)^2), which is o(X^(3/2)). This gives a sufficiently cheap real head near each large scale, even if the untreated individual readings have either sign.
review.local: Guth-Maynard's all-interval Corollary 1.3, not its almost-all corollary, covers lengths from m^(2/3) through m^(3/4) times a fixed log power. Shorter differences are covered by monotonicity. After subtracting the signed tangent the variation costs o(m^(3/2)), allowing all points on the favorable side. Fixed-power choices and the asymptotic threshold are kept separate.
review.critical_price: One twentieth plus the exact small-prime loss 1/24 plus the repeated-power allowance (2/3)(sqrt(8/7)-1) is strictly less than 1/7. Hence success is asserted for the exact existing fourteen-copy prime list, not for an easier substitute.
review.numerics: The 22/7-pi integral estimate and index inequalities are rational. Two sample smoothed readings were also independently evaluated in floating point by ordinary logs and by integration of the genuine prime ramps; these illustrative finite computations are not used to prove the recurrence.
review.openness: Eventually convex off-center comparison functions can also have long good blocks. The assertion that the actual arithmetic fails only finitely often remains unproved. External review and a literature priority check have not been completed.

constants.block_window_in_quartic_indices: [K, 2 K (log(2K))^(1/4)] for all sufficiently large K
